citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., and Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black (MPI for Intelligent Systems, Meshcapade GmbH, York University, MPI for Informatics)
description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based motion capture datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. The dataset contains more than 42 hours of motion data, spanning over 346 subjects, more than 11,451 motions, and provides SMPL pose parameters, body shape parameters, DMPL soft-tissue coefficients, and hand articulations. It is designed to enable machine learning for applications in animation and computer vision.
name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was performed via the MoSh++ automated fitting pipeline. Manual inspection was performed on all results to identify and correct or exclude problematic sequences (e.g., swapped and mislabeled markers). For the SSM dataset, hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation: two of three subjects were used for training and one held out for testing; 20% of mocap files were held out for testing and evaluation.
rai:dataBiases: The source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The dataset unifies 15 existing datasets that each used different markersets and laboratory-specific procedures, which may introduce inconsistencies. The SSM dataset used for hyperparameter tuning consists of only three subjects, limiting the diversity of body shapes used for calibration. The standard 46-markerset was used to determine weights during hyperparameter search, which may bias results for datasets with different marker counts.
rai:dataCollection: 15 existing optical marker-based mocap datasets were collected, some downloaded from the internet (publicly available), others obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, SSM). The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack motion capture system with 24 Prime 17W cameras and 67 reflective markers per subject, synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system capable of 60 fps. MoSh++ was used to map all marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Results were manually inspected and corrected or held out for problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Marker occlusion during mocap sessions was explicitly handled. A missing-marker coefficient q = 1 + (x/|M|)^2.5 was introduced, where x is the number of missing markers in a given frame and |M| is the total number of observed markers. This increases the pose prior weight when more markers are missing, preventing unreliable pose estimates. The coefficient can increase the prior weight by up to a factor of q=3.5 in the worst case.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of sparse optical marker-based motion capture recordings from 15 different datasets, each using different numbers and placements of reflective markers (ranging from 37 to 91 markers per dataset). The SSM dataset additionally includes synchronized high-resolution 4D body scans captured at 60 fps using a 3dMD system with 22 pairs of stereo cameras, 22 color cameras, and 34 speckle projectors.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataImputationProtocol: When hand markers are absent for a subject, hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model. For the first frame of a sequence, the model is initialized by performing a rigid transformation between estimated and observed markers to repose the model from its rest pose.
rai:dataLimitations: Existing mocap databases are limited in size and complexity. The dataset inherits limitations from source datasets including varying markersets and laboratory-specific procedures. MoSh++ runtime is not real-time. The method does not yet handle facial mocap markers. Problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers required manual inspection and correction or exclusion of some sequences.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All 15 source mocap datasets were unified into a common SMPL parameterization using MoSh++. Each frame is represented by SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft-tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions) including hand articulations. The data term weight was automatically scaled by a factor b=46/n to handle varying numbers of markers across datasets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ was applied to convert raw mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters (pose, shape, soft-tissue). The process involves two stages: Stage I estimates body shape and latent marker positions from 12 randomly chosen frames; Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation coefficients for each frame. A missing-marker coefficient q was introduced to handle marker occlusion. Results were manually inspected and problematic sequences (swapped/mislabeled markers) were corrected or excluded.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared. The dataset is available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de.
rai:dataSocialImpact: AMASS enables new applications that require large amounts of human motion training data, supporting advances in computer vision, animation, and robotics. The dataset is made publicly available to the research community to democratize access to large-scale human motion data. The consistent SMPL representation makes it readily useful across many downstream tasks.
rai:dataUseCases: Animation and visualization of human motion; generating training data for deep learning models of human motion; computer vision tasks including human pose estimation; generating synthetic training data for computer vision; character motion synthesis and editing; robotics applications.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (an extension of MoSh) — a model-fitting pipeline using the SMPL/SMPL-H body model and DMPL soft-tissue model to automatically convert sparse mocap marker data into 3D body mesh parameters. Uses Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization implemented in the Chumpy auto-differentiation package.
